headline: Zelenskyy says Starshield speed restrictions were recorded in Ukraine
summary: Ukraine's president says speed restrictions on Starshield were recorded in Ukraine for several days.
Spain's defence ministry is funding a third SpainSat NG satellite for 580 million.
Arianespace plans to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites on the twenty-third of November at the earliest.
Australia's ElevationSpace has signed with Southern Launch for capsule return at the Koonibba Test Range.
The European Space Agency vote of the tenth of November has no published outcome, and the next date is Rome on the fifteenth of December.
bottom_line: The Starshield restrictions in Ukraine are the one pathway that moved today, and no end date has been given. The next date that matters is the twenty-third of November for Ariane 6, then the fifteenth of December in Rome.

global.title: Zelenskyy says Starshield speed restrictions were recorded in Ukraine for several days
global.summary: Ukraine's president says speed restrictions on Starshield service were recorded in Ukraine for several days. The statement was carried on the twelfth of November. An earlier mid-2027 hope for Starshield in Ukraine is unchanged.
global.why: Ukrainian military connectivity depends on a United States provider. The statement adds to the European debate on space sovereignty.
global.bar: Single wire; a Turkish trade headline claiming a Musk order is unsourced and left out.

global.title: NASA makes major contract awards for moon base development
global.summary: NASA has made major contract awards for moon base development, according to Via Satellite on the ninth of November. The headline gives no values or winners. Proposals under the Artemis pathway remain due on the eighth of December.
global.why: The awards show the moon program moving from studies to hardware. Winners and values are not yet in the reading.
global.bar: Headline only; no values or names. Do not state any.

global.title: Arianespace plans Ariane 6 launch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites on twenty-third November at the earliest
global.summary: Arianespace plans to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites on the twenty-third of November at the earliest. It will be the tenth Ariane 6 flight, designated VA271. The Prometheus engine completed a hot-fire test on the sixth of November.
global.why: The flight is a dated test of Ariane 6 cadence. The date is a no-earlier-than date and can move.
global.bar: Company pages count as the company; the date is NET.

items.title: European Space Agency committee vote of tenth November has no published outcome
items.summary: No outcome has been published for the vote of the tenth of November. Rome follows on the fifteenth of December. The agency has opened the tender for Anubis, a planetary defence mission to divert asteroids with ion beams. A European orbiter has detected hints of volcanic activity on Mars.
items.why: The road to Rome depends on the vote result. The Anubis tender is a new procurement.

items.title: TV3 Lietuva describes Russian Starlink counterpart and Ukraine's race against time
items.summary: A Lithuanian report describes a Russian counterpart to Starlink and refers to zombie satellites. It frames Ukraine as racing against time. No date is attached.
items.why: It shows the regional reading of Russian satellite connectivity. The Starshield restrictions give the report fresh context.

items.title: Swedish National Space Agency sets Space Day for eighteenth February 2027
items.summary: The Swedish National Space Agency announced on the second of November that its next Space Day will be held on the eighteenth of February 2027. No other Nordic change is in the reading.
items.why: It is the next dated Swedish agency event. Norway's directorate is running a new national survey of its space sector.

items.title: Spain's defence ministry funds third SpainSat NG satellite with 580 million
items.summary: Spain's defence ministry is funding a third SpainSat NG satellite with 580 million, to replace the damaged NG II. The Spanish Space Agency has taken over management of the Spanish Registry of Space Objects. Seville hosts the NASA Space Apps Challenge on the fourteenth and fifteenth of November.
items.why: The replacement answers a lost satellite. The registry move gives the agency a regulatory role.
items.bar: Currency not stated in the headline.

items.title: Isar Aerospace opens launch window for third Spectrum flight
items.summary: Isar Aerospace has opened the window for the third flight of its Spectrum rocket. The headline gives no date.
items.why: A third flight would extend German small-launch experience. The launch date is not given.

items.title: Turkish trade press says Turkic states' joint satellite will launch in 2027
items.summary: A Turkish trade outlet says a joint satellite of Turkic states will be sent to space in 2027. No launch date is given. The Azercosmos news page could not be loaded.
items.why: It is a standing multinational pathway in Central Asia and the Caucasus. The launch date is the item to watch.

items.title: Türkiye's new microsatellite is set for 2028 and space spending is put at 92 billion liras over three years
items.summary: A Turkish trade outlet says Türkiye's new microsatellite will launch in 2028. It also reports 92 billion liras for space and aviation over three years. The proposal of 24.59 billion liras for 2027 stands.
items.why: The three-year figure frames the annual budget proposal. No split between space and aviation has been published.

items.title: ElevationSpace signs with Southern Launch for capsule return at Koonibba Test Range
items.summary: ElevationSpace has signed with Southern Launch for capsule return at the Koonibba Test Range in South Australia. The headline gives no date for the first return.
items.why: It adds a return-capsule customer to an Australian range. The first return date is not stated.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut to be first foreigner on China's space station
items.summary: A Spanish outlet reports a Pakistani astronaut will be the first foreigner on China's space station. No crew or date is given.
items.why: It would be the first foreign astronaut at the station. The flight date is the item to watch.

items.title: Viasat receives up to 450 million dollars for SDN-B mission operations center
items.summary: Viasat has received a contract worth up to 450 million dollars for the SDN-B Mission Operations Center. Via Satellite carried it on the sixth of November.
items.why: It is a large ground-segment award. Terms beyond the ceiling are not in the reading.

items.title: Venezuela applies satellite and military technology after recent earthquakes
items.summary: teleSUR says Venezuela is applying satellite and military technology in response to risks after recent earthquakes. No date is given.
items.why: It shows satellite imagery used for disaster response in Latin America. The report is a single state-aligned outlet.

audio_script:
Good morning. It is Thursday, the twelfth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Ukraine's president says Starshield speed restrictions were recorded for several days. Spain's defence ministry is funding a third SpainSat NG satellite. And an Australian company has signed for capsule return at the Koonibba range.

Ukraine's president says speed restrictions on Starshield service were recorded in Ukraine for several days. The statement came on the twelfth of November. It bears on how far Ukrainian military connectivity depends on a United States provider. An earlier mid-2027 hope for Starshield in Ukraine is unchanged. We are watching for any explanation or end date.

In Europe, the European Space Agency committee vote of the tenth of November has no published outcome. The next date is Rome on the fifteenth of December. The agency has opened the tender for Anubis, a planetary defence mission to divert asteroids with ion beams. Arianespace plans to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites on the twenty-third of November at the earliest, on the tenth Ariane 6 flight. The Prometheus engine completed a hot-fire test on the sixth of November.

In Lithuania, a TV3 report describes a Russian counterpart to Starlink and refers to zombie satellites. It frames Ukraine as racing against time. No date is attached.

In Sweden, the national space agency has set its next Space Day for the eighteenth of February 2027. That is the next dated Nordic event.

In Spain, the defence ministry is funding a third SpainSat NG satellite, with 580 million, to replace the damaged NG II. The Spanish Space Agency has taken over the Spanish Registry of Space Objects. Seville hosts the NASA Space Apps Challenge on the fourteenth and fifteenth of November. In Germany, Isar Aerospace has opened the window for the third Spectrum flight. No date is given.

In Central Asia and the Turkic world, a joint satellite of Turkic states is due to be launched in 2027. No launch date has been published.

In Türkiye, a new microsatellite is set to launch in 2028. A Turkish trade report puts space and aviation funding at 92 billion liras over three years. The proposal of 24.59 billion liras for 2027 stands, with no split published.

In Australia, ElevationSpace has signed with Southern Launch for capsule return at the Koonibba Test Range. In Pakistan, an astronaut is to be the first foreigner on China's space station. No crew or date has been given.

In the United States, NASA has made major contract awards for moon base development. Proposals under Artemis remain due on the eighth of December. Viasat has received a contract worth up to 450 million dollars for the SDN-B Mission Operations Center. In Venezuela, authorities are applying satellite and military technology after recent earthquakes.

What we are tracking this week is the Starshield restrictions in Ukraine and any outcome from the committee vote of the tenth of November. The Space Apps Challenge in Seville begins on the fourteenth of November. This month, we are tracking the Ariane 6 flight on the twenty-third of November at the earliest, and the Mexicana MRO bid deadline on the same day. Heads-up dates are the eighth of December for Artemis proposals, and the fifteenth of December for Rome. That is the briefing for Thursday, the twelfth of November.

A few closing notes on how to read today's items. The Starshield statement is a single wire report from Anadolu Agency. A Turkish trade headline claiming that Elon Musk ordered Starlink slowed in Ukraine has no named source and no date, so it has been left out of this briefing. Readers should treat the Ukrainian statement as the only confirmed element, and should not infer a cause or an end date.

On Ariane 6, the twenty-third of November is a no-earlier-than date and can move. The company pages count as the company's own word, but a slip of a day or more would not be surprising for a flight of this kind. The NASA moon base awards come from a headline only. No values and no winners have been named, and none should be assumed until NASA or the companies publish them.

On the European Space Agency vote, no outcome is in the reading. Everything about the road to Rome depends on that result, so any publication before the fifteenth of December would be the most important European update of the month.

Finally, several items today rest on a single trade source or a headline alone. These include the Turkic joint satellite, the Turkish microsatellite and the three-year funding figure, the Pakistani astronaut report, and the Venezuelan item from teleSUR, a single state-aligned outlet. They are context, not confirmation. We will update each if a second source or a date appears.

That is all for today. Thank you for listening to the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing.
